newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's judicial workers agree to end strike.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's judicial workers agree to end strike.

text.p: Judicial workers struck a deal on Tuesday to end their strike that has paralysed Colombia's court system a day after the government threatened to break it by declaring a limited state of emergency.

The government granted 40,000 legal workers represented by the ASONAL union a small pay increase, a bonus for length of service and an additional payment to reduce the wage differential with other state sectors. The total accord is roughly equivalent to an 18 percent salary hike.

"The draft agreement on pay has been drawn up. We're just waiting to be called on to sign it," ASONAL leader Antonio Suarez said. He said the 8-day-old strike would be lifted as soon as the final agreement was signed by all sides, possibly later on Tuesday or Wednesday.

Chief prosecutor Alfonso Valdivieso said on Monday that the paralysis of the legal system could force authorities to free all criminals who had missed their court dates because of the strike and cause a "judicial catastrophe."
Justice Minister Carlos Medellin reacted by saying the government could call a limited state of emergency and adopt measures to force the judicial employees back to work.

At least 800,000 other state employees including health and education, oil and telecommunications workers are due to launch a nationwide, indefinite strike on Feb. 11. They are protesting over the 13.5 percent weighted wage rise decreed by the government this month -- well below the 1996 inflation rate of 21.63 percent.
Private sector workers and social organisations say they will also go out on strike if the public sector demands are not met by mid-March.
